description: The pie chart represents the distribution of different levels of ambiguity in a dataset. There are four categories of ambiguity: Std: 0.0, Std: 0.47, Std: 0.82, and Std: 1.0. The Std: 0.0 category has the largest proportion, accounting for 49.0% of the total. The Std: 0.47 category follows with 47.7%, and the Std: 0.82 category has 14.2%. The Std: 1.0 category has the smallest proportion, with 5.0%. The chart is divided into two concentric rings, with the outer ring representing the Ambiguity Std (Outer) and the inner ring representing the Max Ambiguity (Inner). The outer ring has four shades of blue, each corresponding to a different Std value, while the inner ring has three shades of blue, each corresponding to a different Max value. The chart does not include any percentage labels inside the slices or any visual emphasis on any particular slice. The slices appear to be ordered in descending size, starting with the Std: 0.0 category and ending with the Std: 1.0 category.
